chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us: from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Noah (peace be upon him), when it was the days of the Flood, called the waters of the earth, and they answered him, except for the bitter water, and [the] sulphur water.
ai.seo_question: Which two types of water did not obey Prophet Noah during the Flood?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to illustrate the distinct elemental properties preserved during the Deluge, where bitter and sulphur waters remained separate from the sweet waters that obeyed Noah’s call. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the miraculous control of nature by prophets and the preservation of specific natural categories for future utility.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-67 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
Noah (MGB) called all waters to assist him during the Flood. All types of water heeded his call except for two: bitter water and sulphate water.”
